summary: Players race to fill a shrinking reverse-pyramid of cards drafted from a shared river, using color and number combinations to trigger key-based location bonuses and pearl majorities. It plays fast and light, feeling like a puzzly, ever-tightening set-collection sprint rather than a deep strategic contest.
praised: Clever, tense drafting where taking cards for yourself also shapes what's available to opponents
Quick to teach and quick to play at around 30 minutes
Attractive Abyss-universe presentation for fans of the series
Satisfying puzzle of fitting numbers/colors into a shrinking pyramid
criticised: Feels very similar to other games in the Conspiracy system, offering little new if you've played a sibling title
Can feel randomly dependent on what the river offers, especially near the end
Light theme integration — mechanically it's an abstract drafting puzzle wearing Abyss skin
Limited long-term replay depth once the pattern is learned

interaction.kind: open drafting and majority races (pearls, key bonuses) rather than direct conflict

scoring.why: Final score comes from per-color totals modified by location card bonuses and pearl majority bonuses, so it's a handful of interacting sources rather than one simple tally.

similar: Conspiracy: Kutná Hora – The Card Game
